sense: learning and the arts; being cultured

terms.gloss: culture, refinement: the learning and manners that make a person humane
evidence: Cic. Arch. 2: omnēs artēs, quae ad hūmānitātem pertinent
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: mental cultivation befitting a man, liberal education, good breeding, refinement. It also means kindness and human feeling; the context decides. For a people’s civilisation see culture, a people’s way of life.

evidence: M-O s.v. civilized: culture: literary culture
terms.comment: Morgan–Owens’s word for literary culture, from Cicero.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.13: cultūra autem animī philosophia est
Hor. Ep. 1.1.40: sī modo cultūrae patientem commodet aurem
terms.comment: Cicero’s metaphor from farming; Horace uses cultūra alone for it. By itself the word is above all the tilling of land (agrī cultūra), not a people’s culture.

phrases.latin: Etenim omnēs artēs, quae ad hūmānitātem pertinent, habent quoddam commūne vinculum, et quasi cognātiōne quādam inter sē continentur.
phrases.english: For all the arts that belong to culture share a common bond, and are held together by a kind of kinship.

phrases.latin: adde quod ingenuās didicisse fidēliter artēs ēmollit mōrēs nec sinit esse ferōs
phrases.english: besides, to have studied the liberal arts faithfully softens one’s ways and keeps them from being wild

phrases.latin: nēmō adeō ferus est, ut nōn mītēscere possit, sī modo cultūrae patientem commodet aurem
phrases.english: no one is so wild that he cannot be tamed, if only he lends a patient ear to cultivation
